newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty flat vs basket, 1-day depos up on shortage.
newsitem.headline: Zloty flat vs basket, 1-day depos up on shortage.

text.p: The Polish zloty finished a busy day flat against the basket of currencies after it lost ground against the bullish dollar in European trade, but made it up against the mark, dealers said.
They said that the Polish unit should hold its ground against the parity rate tomorrow even if it loses more ground against the bullish dollar.
"If the optimism on the dollar continues on Wednesday, the zloty may fall below 2.8400, but it should stay flat against the basket," said Witold Wozniak from Deutsche Bank in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at 2.13/2.08, flat from Monday's close at 2.11/2.08 percent from parity.
It was at 2.8385/95 to the dollar, down from 2.8243/50 on Monday and at 1.8583/93 to the mark, up from 1.8650/57.
One-day deposit rates have significantly risen on the market's increased borrowing needs in the last week of November's reserve period.

Overnight rates were quoted at 19.20/19.35 percent, up from opening's 19.15/19.30 percent. Tomorrow/next were at 19.30/19.55 percent against 19.20/19.35 percent at 1010 GMT, and the shortage was expected to carry on to Wednesday.

The NBP offered to drain 400 million zlotys off the market for 14-days even though deposit rates on the market of up to two weeks were quoted above the 14-day reverse repo rate of 19.14 percent before the announcement of the operation.
The bank drained 88.6 million zlotys, the amount banks wanted to place, raising the maximum rate to 19.16 percent from 19.14 percent on November 19.

The finance ministry sold 150 million zlotys of one-year index-linked bonds, the amount on offer, after investors bid for 352 million, rising the minimum accepted price to 96.67 from 95.00 at the last auction on October 29. @
The average price also rose to 96.74 from 95.99.
